Dropping an allowed declaration or retaining an extra fixture server fails exact server-set equality; suppressing the anchored editor or retaining another inherited server fails the anchored singleton expectation. Reintroducing a root override for a profile-only server makes the expected empty root map fail; omitting the profile disable or changing its enabled value fails the independently stated nested dictionary. This inspects composed TOML, not installed-harness profile execution.

Restoring missing or true Reckon enabled overrides fails the false-value scans on fresh and resumed Codex argv; adding a fabricated transport for an absent name or omitting a disable for an existing transport fails the conditional literal expected map. Declaring useful in the fixture now makes the retained-useful checks consistent with policy.

The explicit imas-dd flight declaration independently constrains retained servers; restoring unfiltered merge leaves the input run-local fixture present and fails its absence assertion, while removing imas-dd fails its expected fixture declaration.

The fixture at lines 73-75 still supplies operator, so restoring operator retention fails both the expected empty base MCP bytes and the anchored operator-absence check; BASE_MCP is the expected output, not the operator input.

Reinstating the old fallback Reckon override rather than the new empty-table default fails the existing literal full-argv comparisons; production launch_plan additionally supplies computed per-server exclusions, so these assertions only guard dialect composition.
